answer: Each worker on our mesa testnet has to answer a random latency challenge from a fresh relay every hour, and the reply has to come back fast enough to rule out relays on shared hosts. If two IDs answer from the same jetty node, the timing signal shows they share a machine and both lose that week's payouts. A farm with 500 fakes therefore needs 500 separate hosts in separate places, each billed monthly. Renting in bulk doesn't help, because co-located boxes give near-identical round-trip times and get grouped together.
